prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on your goals (social snackable ads, product demos, branded explainers, large-scale automated campaigns), budget, and desired style. Below is a concise guide to the top options and which to pick for common needs.

Top picks (by use case)
- Best for realistic AI presenters / explainer ads: Synthesia or HeyGen
  - Why: photoreal/AI avatars, many languages, script→video, good for corporate/onscreen-presenter style.
  - Good if you need consistent spokespeople, localization, or enterprise features and bulk creation.

- Best for short social ads and repurposing long video content: Pictory, Lumen5, Opus Clip
  - Why: fast script-to-video or long-to-short workflows, auto-subtitles, social-sized outputs and templates.
  - Good if you want to turn blog posts, webinars, or long videos into multiple social clips quickly.

- Best for template-driven, marketing-focused ad creation: InVideo, Promo.com, Shakr
  - Why: large ad template libraries, stock footage/music, easy branding, export presets for Facebook/IG/YouTube.
  - Good if you need polished, platform-optimized ads fast without a big learning curve.

- Best for advanced editing, generative effects and creative freedom: Runway
  - Why: generative video tools, background removal, inpainting, advanced editing — great for standout visuals.
  - Good if you want creative, non-template effects and are comfortable with more hands-on editing.

- Best multi-purpose all-in-one (design + video): Canva / Adobe Express / VEED
  - Why: wide template sets, collaborative features, simple editing, good for teams and frequent small campaigns.
  - Good if you need an easy brand kit, design + video in one place.

- Best for scalable, data-driven ad production and optimization: VidMob, Shakr (enterprise)
  - Why: feed-driven creative, A/B testing and creative analytics, integrations with ad platforms.
  - Good for agencies or e-commerce brands running large ad volumes and creative experiments.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Ad style: avatar presenter vs live-action vs animated vs text-over-stock
- Output needs: vertical/horizontal, resolution, subtitles
- Volume: one-off vs dozens/hundreds of videos
- Localization: how many languages/voices you need
- Brand control: custom fonts, logos, color palette, API or bulk exports
- Budget: hobby/free tier vs enterprise pricing and per-video costs
- Integrations: direct publishing to ad platforms, team collaboration, analytics

Practical next steps
1. Pick 2–3 candidates from the list above that match your use case.
2. Try free trials or generate a single test ad to compare speed, quality, and ease of editing.
3. Evaluate final exports on device(s) and run a small A/B test if possible.

If you tell me: platform (Facebook/Instagram/Reels/YouTube/TikTok), ad length, style (avatar, product demo, text+stock, animated), monthly video volume, and budget, I’ll recommend the single best tool and a concise workflow to produce high-performing ads.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
